lina_k: 🚨 Deploy canary 2026-03-15T10:05 failing in eu-west. Several POST /orders calls returning 500/504. I see the migration job 'add_order_metadata_gencol_backfill' stuck in k8s. paging oncall.
incident-bot: Incident created: sev2 - deploy-canary-db-backfill-block (inc-20260315-58). Notifying on-call.
matt_s: oncall here (matt_s). which pod/job id? logs?
lina_k: job: jobs/backfill-order-meta-20260315-1 in namespace release-canary. logs show `UPDATE orders SET order_meta_gen = ...` has been running for 27m and API latency is spiking. sample:```postgres ERROR: could not obtain lock on relation "orders"
  detail: lock held by PID 9152```
oncall_sre: checking primary pg_stat_activity -> found pid 9152, state = active, query = 'COPY (SELECT ...) TO STDOUT' started by etl/warehouse job at 09:50. It's on a different service but still holding heavyweight lock.
release_eng: oh — our backfill is trying to run concurrently with a warehouse export job; ALTER/UPDATE is blocked. We shipped migration that both adds a generated column and triggers backfill as part of the release job. That backfill should have been throttled.
ops_bot: Current canary traffic: 3% users, error rate on write endpoints 7.2% in eu-west, global effect 0.9%.
product_pm: any paying customers flagged?
support_bot: two support tickets from eu accounts: shoply and orbit-inc reporting order failures since 10:06.
matt_s: propose mitigation: 1) pause canary ramp (stop sending new canary traffic), 2) disable new feature flag for orders so code won't hit generated col path, 3) cancel/stop the backfill job to release locks, 4) re-run migration in controlled mode or rollback. Thoughts?
release_eng: agree. We have kill-switch on flag `orders.meta_v2_enabled` — set to false stops new code path immediately. rollback is `deployctl rollback release/2026-03-15-10` but that won't release DB locks. Need to kill the job on k8s.
oncall_sre: taking handoff. executing: `kubectl -n release-canary delete job backfill-order-meta-20260315-1`
ops_bot: Job deletion requested. Pods terminating.
oncall_sre: verifying pg_locks: `SELECT pid, query, age(clock_timestamp(), query_start) AS running_for FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE pid = 9152;` PID 9152 still running but now in state 'idle' — likely waiting to finish stream. running_for 28m. Trying `SELECT pg_cancel_backend(9152);`
ops_bot: pg_cancel_backend returned true. Query canceled.
release_eng: feature flag toggled: `ffctl set orders.meta_v2_enabled false --reason "mitigate canary hit"`
ops_bot: Feature flag set -> false. Canary ramp paused: `deployctl set-schedule release/2026-03-15-10 --paused true`
lina_k: after cancelling job, migration backfill did not continue automatically (as expected). We re-ran the migration controller in dry-run to ensure safe resume: `./migrate --check add_order_metadata_gencol_backfill` -> ok to run once locks cleared.
matt_s: customer impact: eu-west canary users (3% of traffic) saw write errors for ~20m; support contacted two customers, both non-critical but paying. Recommend reaching out with brief note.
product_pm: I'll draft message for customer ops. keep me in loop.
release_eng: long term fix: split backfill into chunked batches, add pre-flight check for long-running conflicting jobs (WAL streaming / COPY / large exports), and ensure backfill respects cluster maintenance windows. I'll open an RFC + PR to change migration orchestration.
oncall_sre: marking incident mitigated->monitoring. Oncall handover: mira is next oncall and will verify no reoccurrence in next 60m.
incident-bot: Incident inc-20260315-58 status updated: mitigated (paused) -> monitoring, assignee: mira_s.
matt_s: creating short incident note in /incidents/postmortems and tagging release team. timeline summary: 10:05 canary + migration with backfill triggered -> 10:06 locks observed -> 10:09 canary paused and flag off -> 10:12 backfill job killed -> 10:16 errors receded.
support_bot: support tickets updated and customers notified of mitigation and follow-up.
product_pm: suggest we include in postmortem the decision matrix for cancelling DB jobs vs rolling back code.
lina_k: thanks all — handing off to mira_s for post-incident validation and follow up work items (RFC, chunked backfill PR).
